behavior_in_task_description.explanation: instruction.md is deliberately minimal ('Page has this weird zoom effect... happens on more than one of the history pages... they all look like this') and names no files, no thresholds, and not even 'jwtHistory.php' or 'base64history.php'. The tests check exact pages (jwtHistory.php, base64history.php), exact geometry math (scrollWidth/innerWidth <= 1.05), header counts, and row counts -- none of which are specified in the instruction. task.toml's own difficulty_explanation confirms this is intentional ('the issue text mischaracterizes the bug... reading the prose alone points an agent in the wrong direction'), but per the letter of this criterion the instruction does not cover what the tests check.

behavior_in_tests.explanation: The general behavior described in the instruction (a layout/zoom defect affecting more than one history page) is exactly what measure.js verifies: it loads both jwtHistory.php and base64history.php, confirms rows/headers still render (p2p), and asserts each page's scrollWidth stays within 1.05x of the viewport width (f2p). The vague 'more than one page' claim in the instruction maps onto concrete tests for both real affected pages.

informative_test_structure.explanation: test.sh is divided into clearly labeled stages (starting services, seeding DB, DOM-geometry measurement, rubric judge, computing reward) with echoed section headers. measure.js labels each check inline with '// p2p:' / '// f2p:' comments explaining intent, and verifier.py/judge.py carry detailed docstrings explaining the scoring contract, exclusions, and rationale for each step.

anti_cheating_measures.explanation: The task shows unusually deliberate anti-cheat engineering: seed data is created at verifier runtime (not baked into the image or visible to the agent beforehand), thresholds/test file contents are not shipped into the agent's environment, tests/ and solution/ are excluded from the build image, and judge.py explicitly strips test/spec files and withholds the instruction, golden fix.patch, and screenshots from the LLM judge to prevent it from becoming a similarity checker. rubrics.json specifically targets and blocks the three cheating vectors identified during hardening (hardcoded pixel widths, content clipping, harness edits).

structured_data_schema.explanation: The task is a visual/CSS layout bug fix (PHP templates + stylesheets), not one that produces structured output like JSON/CSV/API responses, so a documented output schema is not relevant.

pinned_dependencies.explanation: mariadb-server/mariadb-client are pinned to an exact apt version (1:10.11.18-0+deb12u1), and the npm package playwright is pinned to 1.48.2 both for `npm install` and the matching `npx playwright@1.48.2 install`. Base image php:8.3-bookworm and unpinned apt packages (git, curl, nodejs, npm) are acceptable per the apt-packages-need-not-be-pinned allowance.

typos.explanation: Two issues found: (1) solution/fix.patch adds `border-collapse: collapes;` (misspelled 'collapse') in both new CSS files (CSS/jwtHistory.css and CSS/base64history.css) -- a typo baked into the shipped reference solution. (2) tests/judge.py's docstring claims 'the verifier image is node:22-bookworm', but the only Dockerfile in the task is `FROM php:8.3-bookworm`, and test.sh clearly runs within that same PHP/MariaDB container -- this is a stale/incorrect statement that could mislead anyone maintaining the verifier.

tests_or_solution_in_image.explanation: environment/Dockerfile only COPYs environment/assets/ (the bug screenshot) into the image; it clones the target repo fresh from GitHub at the base commit and never references or copies the tests/ or solution/ directories.

test_deps_in_image.explanation: Playwright and its Chromium browser (pinned 1.48.2, plus `--with-deps chromium`) and Node.js/npm are all installed during the Docker image build (environment/Dockerfile lines 9-16), even though they are exclusively used by tests/measure.js, a test-only script. These are test-only dependencies baked into the image build rather than installed within test.sh at verification time, despite the verifier phase having network_mode="public" and thus the ability to install them on demand.

hardcoded_solution.explanation: solve.sh applies solution/fix.patch, which is the actual upstream code fix (new CSS files plus restructured PHP markup) rather than a shortcut that fabricates or copies expected test output. The verifier then renders the real, patched application through a headless browser and measures live DOM geometry, so the patch must genuinely fix the rendering -- it is not possible to pass by just printing an answer.

file_reference_mentioned.explanation: The tests specifically validate jwtHistory.php, base64history.php, and their new stylesheets (CSS/jwtHistory.css, CSS/base64history.css per task.toml's files_edited), but instruction.md never names any of these files or even the affected page URLs -- it only shows a screenshot of one page and says the defect appears on 'more than one of the history pages' without naming which ones.
